```{r}
#| label: setup

set.seed(20260612)

pacman::p_load(
  here,
  readr,
  dplyr,
  tidyr,
  purrr,
  stringr,
  forcats,
  lubridate,
  broom,
  broom.mixed,
  broom.helpers,
  marginaleffects,
  lme4,
  mgcv,
  binom,
  gtsummary,
  flextable,
  patchwork,
  knitr,
  ggplot2,
  scales
)

theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom"))
set_flextable_defaults(font.size = 9, padding = 3)
theme_gtsummary_compact()

# Factor level orders for display
age_levels <- c("Age under 30", "Age 30-45", "Age over 45")
sex_levels <- c("Female", "Male")
governorate_levels <- c(
  "Deir Al Balah",
  "Gaza City, North Gaza",
  "Khan Yunis, Rafah"
)
role_levels <- c("National staff", "Casual worker", "Other")
chronic_levels <- c("No chronic condition", "Chronic condition")
children_levels <- c("0", "1", "2", "3+")
cohort_levels <- c("Aug-Sep 2025", "Oct-Nov 2025")
bmi_levels <- c("Underweight", "Normal", "Overweight", "Obese")

# Characteristics display order
characteristic_order <- c(
  "age", "sex", "governorate_cat", "children", "role_cat", "chronic",
  "entry_cohort"
)

variable_labels <- c(
  age = "Age group",
  sex = "Sex",
  governorate_cat = "Governorate of residence",
  children = "Dependent children < 10y",
  role_cat = "Professional role",
  chronic = "Chronic condition",
  entry_cohort = "Month of study entry",
  # measured quantities, used by the supplementary tables only
  age_years = "Age (years)",
  bmi_prewar = "Pre-war BMI (kg/m2)",
  bmi_entry = "BMI at entry (kg/m2)",
  pct_weight_change = "Weight change since pre-war (%)"
)

# gtsummary takes labels as a named list, over whichever columns a table shows.
labels_for <- function(variables) as.list(variable_labels[variables])

# 10 October 2025 ceasefire is the breakpoint for the calendar-time model
ceasefire_date <- as_date("2025-10-10")
days_per_month <- 30

# Piecewise calendar-time terms, from days since the start of the study: t_pre
# accumulates until the ceasefire and then stops, t_post accumulates after
# Both in units of 30 days. 
piecewise_terms <- function(calendar_day) {
  break_day <- as.numeric(ceasefire_date - study_start)
  tibble(
    t_pre = pmin(calendar_day, break_day) / days_per_month,
    t_post = pmax(calendar_day - break_day, 0) / days_per_month
  )
}

# pretty formatting helpers
ft <- function(x) {
  flextable(x) |>
    set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1) |>
    theme_booktabs()
}

fmt_ci <- function(estimate, low, high, digits = 1) {
  sprintf(
    paste0("%.", digits, "f (%.", digits, "f to %.", digits, "f)"),
    estimate, low, high
  )
}

fmt_pct <- function(x, digits = 1) sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f%%"), x)

# Individual weight trajectories against calendar time
plot_trajectories <- function(data, subtitle) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = record_date, y = pct_weight_change)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 1, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_line(aes(group = id), alpha = 0.3, colour = "#01454f") +
    geom_point(
      data = \(d) filter(d, !is_first),
      alpha = 0.3, size = 1, colour = "#01454f"
    ) +
    geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, is_first), size = 1.5, colour = "#ffa600") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ceasefire_date, linetype = 2, colour = "grey30") +
    labs(
      x = "Date of measurement",
      y = "Weight relative to pre-war (%)",
      subtitle = subtitle
    )
}

save_fig <- function(plot, name, width = 8, height = 5) {
  dir.create(here("outputs", "figures"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (device in c("png", "pdf")) {
    ggsave(
      here("outputs", "figures", paste0(name, ".", device)),
      plot,
      width = width, height = height, dpi = 300
    )
  }
  plot
}
```

```{r}
#| label: participant-sets

data_processed <- read_csv(
  here("data", "processed", "participants.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

included <- data_processed |>
  filter(record_remove == "include", !is.na(weight)) |>
  mutate(
    record_date = as_date(record_date),
    date_entry = as_date(date_entry),
    entry_cohort = if_else(
      date_entry < as_date("2025-10-01"),
      "Aug-Sep 2025",
      "Oct-Nov 2025"
    ),
    # North Gaza (n = 20) and Rafah (n = 8) are too sparse to estimate
    # separately, so each is combined with its neighbour.
    governorate_cat = case_when(
      governorate %in% c("Gaza City", "North Gaza") ~ "Gaza City, North Gaza",
      governorate %in% c("Khan Yunis", "Rafah") ~ "Khan Yunis, Rafah",
      governorate == "Deir Al Balah" ~ "Deir Al Balah"
    ),
    role_cat = case_when(
      role == "National staff" ~ "National staff",
      role == "Casual/daily worker" ~ "Casual worker",
      is.na(role) ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    # ODK multi-select: "0" = no condition reported, any code = at least one.
    chronic = case_when(
      is.na(chronic_condition) ~ NA_character_,
      chronic_condition == "0" ~ "No chronic condition",
      TRUE ~ "Chronic condition"
    )
  ) |>
  mutate(
    age = factor(age, levels = age_levels),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = sex_levels),
    governorate_cat = factor(governorate_cat, levels = governorate_levels),
    role_cat = factor(role_cat, levels = role_levels),
    chronic = factor(chronic, levels = chronic_levels),
    children = factor(children, levels = children_levels),
    entry_cohort = factor(entry_cohort, levels = cohort_levels)
  ) |>
  add_count(id, name = "n_obs")

study_start <- min(included$record_date)

# Cross-sectional set, one row per participant at entry. 
# Outcome = change from pre-war to first measured weight
baseline <- included |>
  filter(record_number == 1) |>
  mutate(
    pct_weight_change = 100 * (weight_entry - weight_prewar) / weight_prewar,
    bmi_change = bmi_entry - bmi_prewar,
    underweight_prewar = bmi_prewar < 18.5,
    underweight_entry = bmi_entry < 18.5,
    has_followup = n_obs >= 2
  )

cross_sectional <- filter(baseline, !is.na(weight_prewar))

# Longitudinal set: participants with 2+ records
# dropping 2 with implausible between-measurement rate of BMI change (>= 1 kg/m2/day).
longitudinal_all <- included |>
  filter(n_obs >= 2) |>
  arrange(id, record_date) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(
    bmi_daily_change = c(NA, diff(bmi)) / c(NA, as.numeric(diff(record_date)))
  ) |>
  ungroup()

implausible_ids <- longitudinal_all |>
  filter(abs(bmi_daily_change) >= 1) |>
  pull(id) |>
  unique()

# entry_day is a person-level term for the calendar day a participant joined.
longitudinal <- longitudinal_all |>
  filter(!id %in% implausible_ids) |>
  mutate(
    id = factor(id),
    # Same log scale as the association models (the percent form is just back-transformed)
    log_weight_ratio = log(weight / weight_prewar),
    pct_weight_change = 100 * (exp(log_weight_ratio) - 1),
    calendar_day = as.numeric(record_date - study_start),
    days_since_entry = as.numeric(record_date - date_entry),
    entry_day = as.numeric(date_entry - study_start) / days_per_month
  ) |>
  mutate(piecewise_terms(calendar_day)) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(
    is_first = record_date == min(record_date),
    spans_ceasefire = any(record_date <= ceasefire_date) &
      any(record_date > ceasefire_date)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

ceasefire_span <- longitudinal |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(
    pre = any(record_date <= ceasefire_date),
    post = any(record_date > ceasefire_date),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  summarise(
    spanning = sum(pre & post),
    pre_only = sum(pre & !post),
    post_only = sum(!pre & post)
  )
```

## Participation and characteristics

- `r nrow(baseline)` participants were measured at study entry, of whom `r nrow(cross_sectional)` recalled a pre-war weight.
- `r n_distinct(longitudinal_all$id)` returned for at least one further measurement; `r length(implausible_ids)` were dropped for an implausible rate of BMI change, leaving `r n_distinct(longitudinal$id)` in the longitudinal analysis.
- Of those, `r ceasefire_span$spanning` were observed both before and after the 10 October 2025 ceasefire, `r ceasefire_span$pre_only` only before and `r ceasefire_span$post_only` only after.

We re-advertised the study in October 2025, causing a fresh wave of participant recruitment.
However, this meant the participant mix changed over time, so we report and analyse longitudinal results by entry cohort.
We checked for selection bias and report a full comparison of participant differences between the two entry cohorts in the Supplement.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-characteristics
#| tbl-cap: "Characteristics of participants at study entry, by organisation."

baseline |>
  mutate(
    n_observations = n_obs,
    organisation = replace_na(organisation, "Unknown")
  ) |>
  select(
    organisation,
    `Age group` = age,
    Sex = sex,
    `Governorate of residence` = governorate,
    `Professional role` = role,
    `Dependent children < 10y` = children,
    `Chronic condition` = chronic,
    `BMI at entry (kg/m2)` = bmi_entry,
    `Weight observations per participant` = n_observations,
    `Month of first observation` = entry_cohort
  ) |>
  tbl_summary(
    by = organisation,
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "{median} [{p25}-{p75}]",
      all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
    ),
    digits = list(all_continuous() ~ 1, all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1)),
    missing_text = "(Missing)"
  ) |>
  add_overall() |>
  as_flex_table()
```

# Nutritional status at study entry

```{r}
#| label: entry-status

# The two prevalences are measured on the same people, so the difference is
# paired. Bootstrap participants to get its interval.
boot_ci <- function(statistic, n_boot = 2000) {
  quantile(replicate(n_boot, statistic()), c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)
}

paired_underweight <- cross_sectional |>
  filter(!is.na(underweight_prewar), !is.na(underweight_entry))

underweight_rise <- 100 *
  (mean(paired_underweight$underweight_entry) -
     mean(paired_underweight$underweight_prewar))

underweight_rise_ci <- boot_ci(function() {
  i <- sample(nrow(paired_underweight), replace = TRUE)
  100 * (mean(paired_underweight$underweight_entry[i]) -
           mean(paired_underweight$underweight_prewar[i]))
})
```

Underweight prevalence rose by `r fmt_ci(underweight_rise, underweight_rise_ci[[1]], underweight_rise_ci[[2]])` percentage points from pre-war to study entry, on the `r nrow(paired_underweight)` participants with both values (paired bootstrap interval).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-underweight
#| tbl-cap: "Prevalence of WHO underweight, pre-war and at study entry, with Wilson 95% confidence intervals."

prevalence_ci <- function(indicator, label, timeframe) {
  indicator <- indicator[!is.na(indicator)]
  binom.confint(sum(indicator), length(indicator), methods = "wilson") |>
    transmute(
      indicator = label,
      timeframe = timeframe,
      n_positive = x,
      n = n,
      pct = 100 * mean,
      pct_low = 100 * lower,
      pct_high = 100 * upper
    )
}

underweight <- bind_rows(
  prevalence_ci(
    cross_sectional$underweight_prewar,
    "BMI < 18.5 kg/m2 (WHO underweight)",
    "Pre-war (recalled, Oct 2023)"
  ),
  prevalence_ci(
    cross_sectional$underweight_entry,
    "BMI < 18.5 kg/m2 (WHO underweight)",
    "At study entry (measured)"
  )
)
underweight |>
  transmute(
    Indicator = indicator,
    `Reference period` = timeframe,
    `n / N` = paste0(n_positive, " / ", n),
    `% (95% CI)` = fmt_ci(pct, pct_low, pct_high)
  ) |>
  ft()
```

## BMI categories, pre-war to study entry

```{r}
#| label: bmi-categories

bmi_category_long <- cross_sectional |>
  select(
    id,
    entry_cohort,
    sex,
    age,
    `Pre-war` = bmi_category_prewar,
    `Study entry` = bmi_category_entry
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(`Pre-war`, `Study entry`),
    names_to = "period",
    values_to = "bmi_category"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(bmi_category)) |>
  mutate(
    period = factor(period, levels = c("Pre-war", "Study entry")),
    bmi_category = factor(bmi_category, levels = bmi_levels)
  )

# Transition matrix: where each pre-war category ended up at study entry.
bmi_transitions <- cross_sectional |>
  filter(!is.na(bmi_category_prewar), !is.na(bmi_category_entry)) |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(bmi_category_prewar, bmi_category_entry),
      \(x) factor(x, levels = bmi_levels)
    )
  ) |>
  count(bmi_category_prewar, bmi_category_entry, .drop = FALSE) |>
  group_by(bmi_category_prewar) |>
  mutate(pct_of_prewar_category = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-transitions
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Where each pre-war BMI category ended up at study entry.
#|   Columns are pre-war categories and sum to 100%; colour marks the category at study entry, with depth of shade the percentage of the pre-war column.
#|   Grey cells hold no participants.
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5

transitions_plot <- bmi_transitions |>
  mutate(
    bmi_category_entry = fct_rev(bmi_category_entry),
    label = if_else(
      n == 0, "-", sprintf("%d\n%.1f%%", n, pct_of_prewar_category)
    ),
    # Empty cells drop out of the fill scale and are painted by na.value.
    fill_category = if_else(n == 0, NA, bmi_category_entry),
    shade = if_else(n == 0, NA_real_, pct_of_prewar_category)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = bmi_category_prewar, y = bmi_category_entry)) +
  geom_tile(
    aes(fill = fill_category, alpha = shade),
    colour = "white", na.rm = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 3, colour = "grey10") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(
    direction = -1, name = "BMI category at study entry", na.value = "grey85"
  ) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 1), limits = c(0, 100), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Pre-war BMI category", y = "BMI category at study entry")

save_fig(transitions_plot, "fig3-bmi-transitions", width = 7, height = 5)
```

The shift out of the overweight and obese categories is depletion from a high starting point, not an improvement in health.

# Change from pre-war to study entry

```{r}
#| label: descriptive-change

headline <- bind_rows(
  tidy(t.test(cross_sectional$pct_weight_change)) |>
    mutate(outcome = "Weight change since pre-war (%)"),
  tidy(t.test(cross_sectional$bmi_change)) |>
    mutate(outcome = "BMI change since pre-war (kg/m2)")
) |>
  transmute(outcome, n = nrow(cross_sectional), mean = estimate, conf.low, conf.high)

summarise_change <- function(data) {
  data |>
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      across(
        c(pct_weight_change, bmi_change),
        list(mean = \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd = \(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))
      ),
      across(
        pct_weight_change,
        list(
          median = \(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
          p25 = \(x) quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
          p75 = \(x) quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
        )
      ),
      pct_underweight_entry = 100 * mean(underweight_entry, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

descriptive <- bind_rows(
  cross_sectional |>
    summarise_change() |>
    mutate(group = "Overall", .before = 1),
  cross_sectional |>
    group_by(group = as.character(entry_cohort)) |>
    summarise_change()
)
```

# Associations with change since pre-war

The outcome is the log ratio of measured entry weight to recalled pre-war weight, `log(weight_entry / weight_prewar)`.
This is a proportional scale by construction, so the observation that a participant who started heavier has more weight available to lose is handled by the scale rather than by conditioning on a recalled baseline.
Coefficients are back-transformed to percentage differences in weight change relative to the reference level.

Two specifications: `Crude` fits one characteristic at a time, `Adjusted` fits all of them simultaneously.

Reference levels are the most populated stratum of each characteristic, so every comparison is made against the largest group: age 30-45 (n = `r sum(cross_sectional$age == "Age 30-45", na.rm = TRUE)`), female, Khan Yunis and Rafah, no dependent children, national staff, entry Aug-Sep 2025.

Chronic condition is held out of the adjusted model because it was only asked from September 2025 and is missing for `r sum(is.na(cross_sectional$chronic))` of `r nrow(cross_sectional)` participants.
It is reported crude here and, adjusted on the subset who were asked, in the appendix.

```{r}
#| label: associations

exposures <- c(
  "age", "sex", "governorate_cat", "children", "role_cat", "entry_cohort"
)

# Reference level = modal level of each characteristic.
model_data <- cross_sectional |>
  filter(!is.na(weight_prewar), weight_prewar > 0, !is.na(weight_entry)) |>
  mutate(
    log_weight_ratio = log(weight_entry / weight_prewar),
    age = relevel(age, ref = "Age 30-45"),
    governorate_cat = relevel(governorate_cat, ref = "Khan Yunis, Rafah")
  )

# Coefficients are on the log scale; 100 * (exp(b) - 1) is the percentage
# difference in weight relative to the reference level.
as_pct_difference <- function(x) 100 * (exp(x) - 1)

# tidy_plus_plus reads variable and level off the model frame rather than
# parsing them out of the term string, and emits each reference level as a row
# with an estimate of zero, so the comparison every row makes stays visible in
# both the table and the figure.
fit_assoc <- function(data, predictors, model_label,
                      keep_variables = predictors) {
  fit <- lm(reformulate(predictors, response = "log_weight_ratio"), data = data)
  tidy_plus_plus(
    fit,
    conf.int = TRUE,
    intercept = FALSE,
    add_reference_rows = TRUE,
    variable_labels = variable_labels
  ) |>
    filter(variable %in% keep_variables) |>
    transmute(
      model = model_label,
      variable,
      variable_label = var_label,
      level = label,
      reference_row,
      across(c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high), as_pct_difference),
      n_model = stats::nobs(fit)
    )
}

associations <- bind_rows(
  map(
    c(exposures, "chronic"),
    \(exposure) fit_assoc(model_data, exposure, "Crude")
  ) |>
    list_rbind(),
  fit_assoc(model_data, exposures, "Adjusted")
) |>
  mutate(
    model = factor(model, levels = c("Crude", "Adjusted")),
    variable = factor(variable, levels = characteristic_order),
    variable_label = factor(
      variable_label,
      levels = unname(variable_labels[characteristic_order])
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(variable, model)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-associations
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Difference in weight change since pre-war, as a percentage of pre-war weight, by participant characteristic.
#|   Estimates are relative to the most populated level of each characteristic.
#|   North Gaza (n=20) is combined with Gaza City, and Rafah (n=8) with Khan Yunis, both being too sparse to estimate separately.

associations |>
  # Reference levels carry no estimate; they are listed so each comparison
  # states what it is against.
  mutate(
    cell = if_else(
      reference_row, "0 (reference)", fmt_ci(estimate, conf.low, conf.high, 1)
    )
  ) |>
  select(variable, variable_label, level, model, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = cell, values_fill = "-") |>
  transmute(Characteristic = variable_label, Level = level, Crude, Adjusted) |>
  ft()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-forest
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Difference in weight change since pre-war by participant characteristic, as a percentage of pre-war weight.
#|   Hollow points at zero are the reference level of each characteristic.
#|   Negative values indicate greater weight loss than the reference.
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7

forest_data <- associations |>
  filter(variable != "chronic") |>
  mutate(level = fct_rev(fct_inorder(level)))

forest_plot <- forest_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = level, colour = model, shape = reference_row)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_pointrange(
    aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
    size = 0.3
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("Crude" = "#ffa600", "Adjusted" = "#01454f"), name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 1), guide = "none") +
  facet_grid(
    variable_label ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y"
  ) +
  labs(x = "Difference in weight change since pre-war (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside", strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0))

save_fig(forest_plot, "fig5-forest-weight", width = 8, height = 7)
```

# Recovery during follow-up

Among `r n_distinct(longitudinal$id)` participants with two or more measurements (`r nrow(longitudinal)` observations).
The outcome here is weight as a percentage of each participant's own pre-war weight, the same scale as the cross-sectional section, so a slope is the percentage of body weight regained per unit time.
All `r nrow(longitudinal)` longitudinal records carry a pre-war weight, so no one is lost by using it.

```{r}
#| label: fig-trajectories
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Individual trajectories of weight relative to pre-war.
#|   Left: by calendar date, with the 10 October 2025 ceasefire marked.
#|   Right: by time since each participant's own entry, coloured by entry wave.
#|   Filled points are each participant's first measurement.
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5

trajectory_calendar <- plot_trajectories(longitudinal, "Calendar time")

trajectory_entry <- longitudinal |>
  ggplot(aes(x = days_since_entry, y = pct_weight_change, colour = entry_cohort)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 1, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(aes(group = id), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, is_first), size = 1.5) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(direction = -1, name = NULL) +
  labs(
    x = "Days since study entry",
    y = NULL,
    subtitle = "Time in study"
  )

trajectories_plot <- trajectory_calendar + trajectory_entry

save_fig(trajectories_plot, "fig4-trajectories", width = 10, height = 5)
```

## Paired within-person change

```{r}
#| label: fig-trajectories-spanning

#|   These are the same people either side of the break, so a change in their weight cannot be explained by a change in who was measured.
#| fig-width: 8

spanning_plot <- plot_trajectories(
  filter(longitudinal, spans_ceasefire),
  paste(
    ceasefire_span$spanning,
    "participants measured either side of the ceasefire"
  )
)

save_fig(spanning_plot, "fig4b-trajectories-spanning", width = 8, height = 5)
```

```{r}
#| label: paired-change

paired <- longitudinal |>
  filter(entry_cohort == "Aug-Sep 2025") |>
  group_by(id) |>
  filter(max(record_date) > ceasefire_date) |>
  arrange(record_date, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    bmi_diff = last(bmi) - first(bmi),
    pct_diff = last(pct_weight_change) - first(pct_weight_change),
    days_between = as.numeric(last(record_date) - first(record_date)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

paired_change <- bind_rows(
  tidy(t.test(paired$pct_diff)) |>
    mutate(outcome = "Weight, % of pre-war"),
  tidy(t.test(paired$bmi_diff)) |>
    mutate(outcome = "BMI (kg/m2)")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-paired
#| tbl-cap: "Paired within-person change among participants who entered in Aug-Sep 2025 and were measured again after the ceasefire, from first to last measurement."

paired_change |>
  transmute(
    Outcome = outcome,
    N = nrow(paired),
    `Median days between` = median(paired$days_between),
    `Mean change (95% CI)` = fmt_ci(estimate, conf.low, conf.high, 2)
  ) |>
  ft()
```

## Piecewise calendar-time model

Time is measured on the calendar, not from each participant's own entry.
Time-in-study is the wrong axis here: a participant entering in August reaches their day 30 in September while the war continued, and one entering in late October reaches their day 30 in November after the ceasefire, so a single time-in-study slope averages decline and recovery together.

The model is `log(weight / pre-war weight) ~ t_pre + t_post + entry_day + (1 | id)`, the same log scale as the association models above, with coefficients back-transformed to percent change in weight.
Where `t_pre` accumulates until 10 October 2025 and then stops, `t_post` accumulates only after it, and `entry_day` is the calendar day a participant joined.

Time is scaled in units of 30 days because a month is the interval the manuscript reports and it puts the coefficients on a readable scale; the same slope per week is the reported value divided by `r sprintf("%.2f", days_per_month / 7)`, and nothing about the model changes with the choice.

`(1 | id)` gives each participant their own intercept, so the slopes are estimated from change within participants rather than from differences between them.
Random slopes would additionally let each participant have their own rate of change, but `r sum(table(longitudinal$id) == 2)` of `r n_distinct(longitudinal$id)` participants contribute exactly two measurements and `r sum(table(longitudinal$id) == 3)` contribute three; two points determine a line exactly, so there is no information left to estimate how much individual rates vary around the average.

Age and governorate are not adjusted for, and adjusting for them would change nothing: they are fixed within a participant, so with a participant-level intercept they cannot confound a within-person slope.
They matter only if they modify the slope, which is what the age interaction below tests.

`entry_day` is the one time-constant term that is included, because it is not fixed by design but by when someone happened to join, and it lets a later-joining participant sit at a different level without that difference being absorbed into the time slopes.
It cannot resolve the confounding between entry wave and ceasefire period and should not be read as doing so.
The fit without it is reported in the sensitivity table.

```{r}
#| label: longitudinal-models

fit_piecewise <- lmer(
  log_weight_ratio ~ t_pre + t_post + entry_day + (1 | id),
  data = longitudinal
)

slopes <- tidy(fit_piecewise, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) |>
  filter(term %in% c("t_pre", "t_post")) |>
  transmute(
    term = if_else(
      term == "t_pre",
      "Before the ceasefire (to 10 Oct 2025)",
      "After the ceasefire (from 10 Oct 2025)"
    ),
    across(c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high), as_pct_difference)
  )

# Difference between the two slopes: a linear contrast on the fixed effects.
slope_difference <- hypotheses(fit_piecewise, "t_post - t_pre = 0") |>
  tidy() |>
  transmute(
    term = "Difference (after relative to before)",
    across(c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high), as_pct_difference)
  )

# On the log scale the random-intercept and residual SDs are multiplicative;
# back-transformed they are approximate percentages of a participant's own
# pre-war weight.
variance_components <- tidy(fit_piecewise, effects = "ran_pars") |>
  transmute(
    component = if_else(
      group == "id", "Between participants", "Within participant (residual)"
    ),
    estimate = as_pct_difference(estimate)
  )

# Sensitivity: the same model without the entry-day term.
fit_no_entry_day <- lmer(
  log_weight_ratio ~ t_pre + t_post + (1 | id),
  data = longitudinal
)

# Effect modification by age group.
fit_piecewise_age <- lmer(
  log_weight_ratio ~ (t_pre + t_post) * age + entry_day + (1 | id),
  data = longitudinal
)

slopes_age <- tidy(fit_piecewise_age, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) |>
  filter(str_detect(term, "t_pre|t_post")) |>
  transmute(term, across(c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high), as_pct_difference))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-slopes
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Change in weight per 30 days, as a percentage of current weight, before and after the 10 October 2025 ceasefire.
#|   Coefficients are back-transformed from the log scale, so the difference row is the percentage by which the post-ceasefire rate of change exceeds the pre-ceasefire one.
#|   Wald 95% confidence intervals.

bind_rows(slopes, slope_difference) |>
  transmute(
    Term = term,
    `Weight change per 30 days, % (95% CI)` = fmt_ci(
      estimate, conf.low, conf.high, 2
    )
  ) |>
  ft()
```

Weight was rising in both periods.
The difference between the two slopes is a separate question, and the data do not settle it: the interval on the difference spans zero.
Recovery was already underway before 10 October, and while the point estimate is larger afterwards, this study cannot establish that the ceasefire changed the rate.
Reporting the pre-ceasefire slope is what makes that visible.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-variance
#| tbl-cap: "Variance components of the piecewise model, back-transformed from the log scale to approximate percentages of body weight."

variance_components |>
  transmute(Source = component, `SD (% of body weight)` = sprintf("%.2f", estimate)) |>
  ft()
```

The two standard deviations split the variation the model does not explain by time.
The between-participant term is how far apart participants sit from each other once the time trend is removed: participants differ by roughly this much in how depleted they were relative to their own pre-war weight.
The within-participant term is how far a single measurement falls from that participant's own fitted line, so it covers real short-term fluctuation plus scale and recording error.
The between-participant term being much the larger is why a participant-level intercept is needed at all, and why the slopes are worth estimating within person.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-slope-age
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Effect modification of the slopes by age group, per 30 days, reference age under 30.
#|   The first two rows are the reference slopes; the rest are differences from them.

slopes_age |>
  transmute(
    Term = term |>
      str_replace("^t_pre$", "Before ceasefire, age under 30 (reference)") |>
      str_replace("^t_post$", "After ceasefire, age under 30 (reference)") |>
      str_replace("t_pre:age", "Before ceasefire, difference for ") |>
      str_replace("t_post:age", "After ceasefire, difference for "),
    `Weight change per 30 days, % (95% CI)` = fmt_ci(
      estimate, conf.low, conf.high, 2
    )
  ) |>
  ft()
```

## Model fit and a smooth alternative

The piecewise model imposes a single break at 10 October.
A generalised additive model with a smooth of calendar day and the same participant random intercept imposes no break, so comparing the two shows whether the recovery actually bends where the ceasefire is.

```{r}
#| label: gam-sensitivity

fit_gam <- gam(
  log_weight_ratio ~ s(calendar_day) + s(id, bs = "re"),
  data = longitudinal,
  method = "REML"
)

prediction_grid <- tibble(
  calendar_day = seq(
    min(longitudinal$calendar_day), max(longitudinal$calendar_day),
    by = 1
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    record_date = study_start + calendar_day,
    entry_day = mean(longitudinal$entry_day),
    id = longitudinal$id[1]
  ) |>
  mutate(piecewise_terms(calendar_day))

# Both fits are on the log scale; the figure plots weight relative to pre-war,
# so predictions and interval bounds are back-transformed. The random effect is
# held out of both, by the argument each package uses for it.
predict_population <- function(model, model_label, ...) {
  predictions(model, newdata = prediction_grid, ...) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(
      record_date,
      model = model_label,
      across(c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high), as_pct_difference)
    )
}

model_fits <- bind_rows(
  predict_population(fit_piecewise, "Piecewise (primary)", re.form = NA),
  predict_population(
    fit_gam, "Smooth of calendar day (GAM)", exclude = "s(id)"
  )
)

gam_summary <- summary(fit_gam)
gam_edf <- gam_summary$s.table["s(calendar_day)", "edf"]

# The comparison that answers the entry-day question is what the slopes do when
# it is removed, not a fit statistic: AIC is not comparable across these fits,
# since the two lme4 models differ in fixed effects under REML and the GAM
# handles its random effect differently again.
slope_row <- function(fit, label) {
  tidy(fit, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) |>
    filter(term %in% c("t_pre", "t_post")) |>
    transmute(
      Specification = label,
      term = if_else(term == "t_pre", "Before ceasefire", "After ceasefire"),
      value = fmt_ci(
        as_pct_difference(estimate),
        as_pct_difference(conf.low),
        as_pct_difference(conf.high),
        2
      )
    ) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = value)
}

model_comparison <- bind_rows(
  slope_row(fit_piecewise, "Piecewise, with entry day (primary)"),
  slope_row(fit_no_entry_day, "Piecewise, without entry day")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-model-fit
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Fitted population-level trajectory from the piecewise model and from the GAM smooth, over the observed data.
#|   Bands are 95% confidence intervals on the fitted mean, with the participant random effect held out of both.
#|   Dashed line is the ceasefire.
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

model_fit_plot <- ggplot(mapping = aes(x = record_date)) +
  geom_line(
    data = longitudinal,
    aes(y = pct_weight_change, group = id),
    alpha = 0.15, colour = "#01454f"
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = model_fits,
    aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high, fill = model),
    alpha = 0.2, colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_line(data = model_fits, aes(y = estimate, colour = model), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = ceasefire_date, linetype = 2, colour = "grey30") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Piecewise (primary)" = "#ffa600",
      "Smooth of calendar day (GAM)" = "#7a5195"
    ),
    name = NULL,
    aesthetics = c("colour", "fill")
  ) +
  labs(x = "Date of measurement", y = "Weight relative to pre-war (%)")

save_fig(model_fit_plot, "fig6-model-fit", width = 8, height = 5)
```

The smooth uses `r sprintf("%.1f", gam_edf)` effective degrees of freedom.
A value of 1 is a straight line: given this data the smooth finds no curvature to fit anywhere, at the ceasefire or elsewhere.
That is the honest summary of the recovery signal here.
The piecewise model does not contradict it, because the difference between its two slopes already spans zero; the break at 10 October is a question the study was designed to ask, not a feature the data insist on.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-model-comparison
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   What the entry-day term does to the slopes, as percent weight change per 30 days.
#|   Fit statistics are not compared: the two models differ in their fixed effects and are fitted by REML, under which AIC is not comparable.

model_comparison |> ft()
```

Dropping `entry_day` moves the slopes very little, which is what should be expected: it is fixed within a participant, so with a participant-level intercept it has little room to act.
It is retained because it is the one time-constant term not fixed by design, and reporting the fit without it is cheaper than arguing about it.

```{r}
#| label: external-comparison

# The aggregated file carries means only, so SDs for the published column would
# have to come from the paper: flagged rather than fabricated.
survey_2020 <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "gaza_survey2020_kcal_bmi_agg.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  transmute(
    age_band = age_cat,
    sex = if_else(gender == "f", "Female", "Male"),
    bmi_2020 = weight / height^2
  )

external_comparison <- cross_sectional |>
  filter(!is.na(age_years), age_years >= 40, !is.na(bmi_prewar)) |>
  mutate(
    age_band = cut(
      age_years,
      breaks = c(40, 50, 60, 70, 120),
      right = FALSE,
      labels = c("[40,50)", "[50,60)", "[60,70)", "[70,120]")
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(age_band, sex) |>
  summarise(
    n_this_study = n(),
    mean_bmi_prewar = mean(bmi_prewar),
    sd_bmi_prewar = sd(bmi_prewar),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(age_band = as.character(age_band), sex = as.character(sex)) |>
  left_join(survey_2020, by = c("age_band", "sex"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-external

external_comparison |>
  transmute(
    `Age band` = age_band,
    Sex = sex,
    `This study, n` = n_this_study,
```

The aggregated 2020 file carries means only.
SDs for the published column have to come from the paper or from whoever holds the microdata.

# Supplement

## Data quality

### Exclusion criteria

Weight data come from two ODK survey forms: `form1`, the baseline enrolment record carrying all characteristics, and `form2`, a follow-up record carrying date and weight only, identified by participant's choice of anonymised ID.
Around 200 `form2` records could not be matched to any `form1` participant ID, so they have no pre-war weight, height or demographics.
These may be participants who only ever used the follow-up form, or participants who enrolled at baseline and then entered a different ID combination.

```{r}
#| label: exclusions

exclusions <- read_csv(
  here("data", "processed", "data-quality.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-exclusions
#| tbl-cap: >-
#|   Records assessed against each exclusion criterion in turn.
#|   Records passing all criteria are labelled `include`.

exclusions |>
  transmute(
    `Record processing` = reason,
    Label = record_remove,
    Records = n_records,
    Participants = n_participants,
    `Records remaining` = n_remaining,
    `Participants remaining` = n_participants_remaining
  ) |>
  ft()
```

### Selection and measurement checks

#### Participant recall: digit preference in recalled pre-war weight

Recalled pre-war weight against measured weight at entry.
Both are heaped on whole kilograms, so the measured value is not a clean reference: scales and recorders round too.
The excess heaping in the recalled value over the measured one is what quantifies how much coarser recall was.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-digits
#| tbl-cap: "Rounding in recalled pre-war weight compared with measured weight at entry."

is_whole_kg <- function(weight) abs(weight - round(weight)) < 1e-8

cross_sectional |>
  select(id, Recalled = weight_prewar, Measured = weight_entry) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Recalled, Measured), names_to = "source", values_to = "weight") |>
  filter(!is.na(weight)) |>
  group_by(source) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    pct_whole_kg = 100 * mean(is_whole_kg(weight)),
    pct_ends_0_or_5_kg = 100 * mean(is_whole_kg(weight) & round(weight) %% 5 == 0),
    pct_ends_0_kg = 100 * mean(is_whole_kg(weight) & round(weight) %% 10 == 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Source = source,
    N = n,
    `Whole kg` = fmt_pct(pct_whole_kg),
    `Ends in 0 or 5 kg` = fmt_pct(pct_ends_0_or_5_kg),
    `Ends in 0 kg` = fmt_pct(pct_ends_0_kg)
  ) |>
  ft()
```

### Participant selection

We consider selection bias by reporting distributions of baseline characteristics across subgroups.
We looked at differences between participants providing one, or multiple measurements over time.

```{r}
#| label: set-up-balance-table

balance_vars <- c(
  "age", "sex", "governorate_cat", "children", "role_cat",
  "age_years", "bmi_prewar", "bmi_entry", "pct_weight_change"
)

balance_table <- function(data, group_var) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[group_var]])) |>
    select(all_of(c(group_var, balance_vars))) |>
    tbl_summary(
      by = all_of(group_var),
      label = labels_for(balance_vars),
      statistic = list(
        all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})",
        all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
      ),
      digits = list(all_continuous() ~ 1, all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1)),
      missing_text = "(Missing)"
    ) |>
    as_flex_table()
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-balance-followup
#| tbl-cap: "Baseline characteristics by whether the participant contributed any follow-up measurement."

baseline |>
  mutate(
    followup = factor(
      if_else(has_followup, "2+ observations", "Single observation"),
      levels = c("Single observation", "2+ observations")
    )
  ) |>
  balance_table("followup")
```

We formalise this view by modelling the odds of contributing any follow-up, by participant characteristic (age, sex, governorate, dependents, role, BMI at entry, and entry cohort), using a binomial GLM.
<!-- TODO: do we need this as well as the balance table above? -->

```{r}
#| label: tbl-return
#| tbl-cap: "Odds of contributing at least one follow-up measurement, by participant characteristic at entry."

glm(
  has_followup ~ age + sex + governorate_cat + children + role_cat +
    bmi_entry + entry_cohort,
  data = baseline,
  family = binomial()
) |>
  tbl_regression(
    exponentiate = TRUE,
    label = labels_for(c(
      "age", "sex", "governorate_cat", "children", "role_cat",
      "bmi_entry", "entry_cohort"
    ))
  ) |>
  modify_column_hide("p.value") |>
  as_flex_table()
```

#### Entry cohorts

We also considered differences in the participant mix between entry cohorts.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-balance-cohort
#| tbl-cap: "Baseline characteristics by entry cohort."

balance_table(baseline, "entry_cohort")
```

## Chronic conditions

Chronic condition was only asked from September 2025.
This model restricts to the participants who were asked and adjusts for the same characteristics as the main adjusted model.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-chronic
#| tbl-cap: "Difference in weight change since pre-war for participants reporting a chronic condition, adjusted, among those who were asked."

# Chronic condition, adjusted, restricted to participants who were asked.
chronic_adjusted <- fit_assoc(
  filter(model_data, !is.na(chronic)),
  c(exposures, "chronic"),
  "Adjusted (restricted to those asked)",
  keep_variables = "chronic"
)

chronic_adjusted |>
  filter(!reference_row) |>
  transmute(
    Level = level,
    `Difference (95% CI), %` = fmt_ci(estimate, conf.low, conf.high, 1),
    N = n_model
  ) |>
  ft()
```
